statement: An eq or prefix with ignoreCase whose literal holds a character beyond ASCII that has another case does not compile where a miss lets a request through: in a DENY statement's condition under an even number of nots, in an ALLOW statement's condition under an odd number, in a rate limit rule's condition as in a DENY, and in a policy condition in both directions its statements give it (under an even number of nots when the policy has a DENY, under an odd number when it has an ALLOW). The fold is ASCII only, so such an atom matches fewer spellings than it reads. The message names a spelling the fold misses and says to list every spelling in an in (eq) or an or of prefixes (prefix), without ignoreCase. In the other direction the atom only narrows: it compiles, and the control plane's validation reports a WARNING. cosec-migrate refuses the same shape with the same message.
guards: model:ConditionLintsTest#ignoreCase on a letter beyond ASCII refuses where a miss lets a request through
